rationale:
Evidence from iteration 6 (sensors at y = 0.08, kd 0.5, kp 3.5, base_speed 1.6, line_loss search_right): score 63.05, below iteration 4's 64.17 and iteration 5's 64.01. Every trial still went off track. max_error was 0.0624 (oval), 0.0632 (s-bend) and 0.0645 (slalom), no better than at y = 0.07. Line-loss events stayed at 1 per run, and steering_oscillation was 0.109 (oval), 0.147 (s-bend) and 0.154 (slalom). Moving the sensor row from 0.07 to 0.08 gave no gain, so the forward-row lever has reached its limit. Following the Evaluator's rule (score below 64.17 with no max_error gain), I return the sensor row to y = 0.07, the best-measured position.

I also revert line_loss to last_direction, the setting from iteration 4 (64.17). search_right in iteration 5 changed the score by only -0.16, so it had no measurable effect. Iteration 4 is therefore the clean baseline.

Change: with the baseline restored, the single variable I test is controller.kd, raised from 0.5 to 0.8. Iterations 3 to 4 showed that raising kd from 0.3 to 0.5 cut oval oscillation and gained about 1.5 points, and max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 m since then. Geometry, kp 3.5, base_speed 1.6 and sensor_size 0.012 are all unchanged.

Expected result: max_error falls toward or below 0.06 m, steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.15, and the score is at or above 64.17. Hypotheses: (H1) more damping reduces the overshoot on the bends that causes the single line-loss event, so max_error drops by a few mm; (H2) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 on the s-bend and slalom, the derivative is amplifying sensor noise, so the next step is kd 0.6 rather than higher. (H3) If max_error stays at 0.061 to 0.065 m, controller-side damping is exhausted; the remaining levers are base_speed (lower speed to reduce bend overshoot, at the cost of completion time) or kp (2.5 to reduce over-steer). Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation.
